The .deb / .rpm files on https://opencode.ai/download are OpenCode Desktop bundles. Pre-1.14.34, Desktop ran on Tauri and bundled the CLI/TUI binary at /usr/bin/opencode-cli because the Desktop frontend needed a local server. 1.14.34 (#19067) moved Desktop to Electron, which runs the server in Node, so the bundled CLI was no longer needed and got dropped. The CLI inside the Desktop bundle not intended install path for the TUI on Linux.

If you just want to install opencode on Linux

```
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
```

or if package managers have it:

```
paru -S opencode
```

or npm style:

```
npm i -g opencode-ai
```

or the static binary releases (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases) and add to $PATH. 

There's no first-party Debian/RPM packaging today, but the path to add one is roughly:

Repack the prebuilt tarball. same approach as the AUR opencode-bin and Homebrew formulas.
   - Source: `https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/download/v<version>/opencode-linux-<x64|arm64>[-baseline][-musl].tar.gz`
   - Install: `install -Dm755 ./opencode /usr/bin/opencode`
   - Declare Depends: ripgrep / Requires: ripgrep. Without it, opencode downloads ripgrep from GitHub on first use
   - SHA-256s are published only for opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz and opencode-linux-arm64.tar.gz. Compute your own for -baseline / -musl.
   - Disable self-upgrade

Or build from source.

I've identified a few areas that should be improved before merging:

1. **Error Handling**: The code doesn't properly handle potential errors during MorphClient initialization in 

2. **Authentication Logic**: The dual authentication approach (checking both Auth.get('morph') and Env.get('MORPH_API_KEY')) could be clarified or simplified.

Adding another data point: this regression also affects in-process plugin event delivery (via `bus.subscribeAll()`), not just the external SSE `/event` stream.

I have a server-side plugin that subscribes to bus events to drive a status reporter. Bisecting between v1.14.41 (works) and v1.14.42 (broken) — identical to @lokikl's bisect — I captured exactly which events the plugin's event handler receives:

**v1.14.41 — outer event types seen by `bus.subscribeAll()`:**
```
message.part.delta
message.part.updated
message.updated
session.created
session.diff, session.idle, session.status, session.updated, tui.toast.show
```
**v1.14.42 — outer event types seen by `bus.subscribeAll()`:**
```
message.part.delta
session.diff, session.idle, session.status, session.updated, tui.toast.show
```

Missing in v1.14.42: `message.part.updated`, `message.updated`, `session.created`.

The session data is still correctly persisted — `GET /session/{id}/message` returns the full assistant message with step-start, text, step-finish parts — but the bus never announces those parts to plugin subscribers. Net effect: any plugin that drives state machines off `message.part.updated` (step-start / text / reasoning / tool / step-finish) stops working silently.

#26936 ("fix(tui): scope events by project", merged into dev today) appears to address the TUI side via a new event-subscription API with metadata, but it doesn't change `bus.subscribeAll()`, which is what plugins (and any non-TUI subscriber) use. Just flagging so the in-process plugin case isn't missed when the fix lands.
